part: The foundation, taught in full depth: language basics, OOP, exceptions, generics, collections, functional Java, I/O and build tools.
t: Core Java 1: language basics and OOP
d: The JVM, types, strings and control flow, then classes, the four pillars of OOP, and the Object contract.

topics.t: JDK vs JRE vs JVM; install JDK 21 (Eclipse Temurin), IntelliJ IDEA Community
Primitive types, wrapper classes, autoboxing, type casting
topics.sub: int vs Integer, Integer cache (-128 to 127)

topics.t: Operators, control flow, loops, switch expressions
Arrays (1D/2D), Arrays utility class
Strings: immutability, string pool, StringBuilder vs StringBuffer, common methods, text blocks
Packages, imports, classpath, the main method, var (local type inference)
Classes, objects, constructors, constructor chaining, this & super
Encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction (the 4 pillars)
topics.sub: With real examples, not just definitions

topics.t: Method overloading vs overriding, dynamic dispatch, covariant return types
Abstract classes vs interfaces (default, static, private methods)
static and final keywords; static blocks; access modifiers
Inner, static nested, local and anonymous classes
Object class methods: equals(), hashCode() contract, toString(), clone()
Immutable classes; composition vs inheritance
Enums (with fields & methods), records, sealed classes

part: The foundation, taught in full depth: language basics, OOP, exceptions, generics, collections, functional Java, I/O and build tools.
t: Core Java 2: exceptions, generics and collections
d: Handling errors properly, writing type-safe generic code, and the collections every Java interview asks about.

topics.t: Exception hierarchy: Throwable, Error, checked vs unchecked
try-catch-finally, multi-catch, try-with-resources, AutoCloseable
throw vs throws, custom exceptions, exception chaining
Best practices: don't swallow exceptions, use specific exceptions, log properly
Generic classes & methods, bounded types (<T extends Number>)
Wildcards: ?, ? extends, ? super (PECS rule)
Type erasure and its limitations
Collection hierarchy: List, Set, Queue, Deque, Map
ArrayList vs LinkedList (internals & Big-O)
HashSet, LinkedHashSet, TreeSet
HashMap internals: hashing, buckets, collisions, treeification (Java 8+), load factor, resizing
topics.sub: Asked in almost every Java interview

topics.t: LinkedHashMap (LRU cache), TreeMap, EnumMap, WeakHashMap, IdentityHashMap
PriorityQueue (heap), ArrayDeque (stack/queue)
Comparable vs Comparator; Comparator.comparing().thenComparing()
Iterator, ListIterator; fail-fast vs fail-safe iterators
Collections & Arrays utility methods; immutable collections (List.of, Map.of)
Sequenced collections (Java 21): getFirst(), getLast(), reversed()

part: The foundation, taught in full depth: language basics, OOP, exceptions, generics, collections, functional Java, I/O and build tools.
t: Core Java 3: functional Java, I/O and build tools
d: Lambdas, streams, collectors, Optional and dates, then files, JSON, money with BigDecimal, Maven and Gradle.

topics.t: Lambda expressions & functional interfaces (Function, Predicate, Consumer, Supplier, BiFunction)
Method references
Streams API: map, filter, reduce, collect, sorted, distinct, limit, flatMap
Collectors: groupingBy, partitioningBy, toMap, joining, counting, summingInt
topics.sub: Practise a lot: common live-coding questions

topics.t: Lazy evaluation, intermediate vs terminal operations, parallel streams & their pitfalls
Optional: correct usage and anti-patterns
Date/Time API: LocalDate, LocalDateTime, Instant, ZonedDateTime, Duration, DateTimeFormatter
topics.sub: Time zones matter in real apps

topics.t: File I/O, NIO.2 (Path, Files), reading CSV files
Serialization basics; JSON with Jackson (ObjectMapper, annotations)
BigDecimal for money (never double!), rounding modes
topics.sub: Needed for prices and any exact decimal maths

topics.t: Maven: pom.xml, lifecycle, dependencies & scopes, plugins, multi-module
Gradle basics (read and modify a build.gradle)

part: Advanced Java, SQL, Spring Boot, microservices and Kafka.
d: What separates a Java developer from someone who knows Java syntax. Concurrency and JVM questions come up in most Java interviews.

topics.t: Process vs thread; Thread, Runnable, Callable; thread lifecycle & states
synchronized (methods/blocks), intrinsic locks, volatile, happens-before
Java Memory Model, visibility & atomicity problems, race conditions
wait/notify, producer-consumer problem
Deadlock, livelock, starvation: causes and prevention
Locks: ReentrantLock, ReadWriteLock, StampedLock, Condition
Atomic classes (AtomicInteger, LongAdder), CAS
ExecutorService, thread pools (fixed, cached, scheduled), ThreadPoolExecutor parameters
Future, CompletableFuture (thenApply, thenCompose, allOf, exception handling)
Concurrent collections: ConcurrentHashMap, CopyOnWriteArrayList, BlockingQueue
Synchronizers: CountDownLatch, CyclicBarrier, Semaphore, Phaser
ForkJoinPool & work stealing; ThreadLocal
Virtual threads (Java 21): what they are, when to use, pinning
Structured concurrency & scoped values (newer Java)
Class loading: bootstrap, platform, application class loaders; delegation model
JVM memory: heap (young/old), stack, metaspace, code cache
Garbage collection: mark-sweep, generational GC, G1, ZGC; GC roots
JIT compilation, bytecode basics (javap)
Memory leaks in Java, OutOfMemoryError & StackOverflowError causes
Profiling & diagnosis: heap dumps, thread dumps, VisualVM, JFR, JDK Mission Control
Common JVM flags: -Xms, -Xmx, -XX:+UseG1GC
Records, sealed classes, pattern matching for instanceof
Switch expressions & pattern matching for switch, record patterns
Text blocks, enhanced NullPointerException messages
Java 21: virtual threads, sequenced collections, record patterns
Java 25: compact source files & instance main methods, flexible constructor bodies, scoped values, module imports
Java modules (JPMS): awareness level
Reflection API basics, how frameworks like Spring use it
Built-in & custom annotations, retention policies
Dynamic proxies (JDK proxy vs CGLIB): foundation of Spring AOP
JDBC: DriverManager, Connection, PreparedStatement, ResultSet, batch updates
Transactions in JDBC, connection pooling (HikariCP), SQL injection prevention
Logging: SLF4J + Logback, log levels, structured logging, MDC

part: Advanced Java, SQL, Spring Boot, microservices and Kafka.
d: You already use SQL at work. Make it excellent: SQL rounds are common and you can stand out here.

topics.t: Tables, primary/foreign/composite/surrogate keys, constraints (UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK)
Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF) and when to denormalize
ER modeling: one-to-one, one-to-many, many-to-many (join tables)
SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT/OFFSET, DISTINCT, LIKE, IN, BETWEEN
Aggregates & GROUP BY, HAVING vs WHERE
JOINs: inner, left, right, full outer, self, cross
topics.sub: Classic: find rows in A that are missing in B with LEFT JOIN … IS NULL

topics.t: Subqueries, correlated subqueries, EXISTS vs IN
CTEs (WITH), recursive CTEs (hierarchies)
Window functions: ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG/LEAD, running totals, PARTITION BY
CASE expressions, NULL handling (COALESCE, NULLIF), set operators (UNION, INTERSECT, EXCEPT)
String & date functions
CREATE/ALTER/DROP; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE; DELETE vs TRUNCATE vs DROP
UPSERT (INSERT … ON CONFLICT / MERGE)
Views, materialized views, stored procedures, functions, triggers
Indexes: B-tree, composite, covering, unique; when an index is not used
Clustered vs non-clustered indexes
Reading EXPLAIN / EXPLAIN ANALYZE query plans
Query optimization habits; keyset vs offset pagination; partitioning large tables
ACID properties
Isolation levels: read uncommitted, read committed, repeatable read, serializable
Anomalies: dirty read, non-repeatable read, phantom read, lost update
Locking: row/table locks, optimistic vs pessimistic, deadlocks; MVCC
PostgreSQL (learn this) and MySQL; awareness of Oracle (common in large enterprises)
NoSQL types: document (MongoDB), key-value (Redis), wide-column (Cassandra)
Redis for caching, sessions, rate limiting
CAP theorem, SQL vs NoSQL tradeoffs

part: Advanced Java, SQL, Spring Boot, microservices and Kafka.
d: The heart of the backend. Learn how Spring works underneath (IoC, proxies, auto-configuration), not only the annotations.

topics.t: Inversion of Control & Dependency Injection (constructor vs setter vs field injection)
ApplicationContext, BeanFactory, bean definition
Stereotypes: @Component, @Service, @Repository, @Controller; @Configuration + @Bean
@Autowired, @Qualifier, @Primary; resolving multiple beans
Bean scopes (singleton, prototype, request, session) and bean lifecycle (@PostConstruct, @PreDestroy)
Profiles, @Value, @ConfigurationProperties, externalized configuration
Spring AOP: aspects, advice types, pointcuts, how proxies work
Circular dependencies & how to avoid them
Spring Initializr, starters, project structure
How auto-configuration works (@Conditional…, @SpringBootApplication breakdown)
application.yml/properties, profiles, environment-specific config
Embedded server, executable JAR, DevTools
Actuator: health, metrics, info endpoints
Logging configuration
Boot 2 → 3 → 4 changes: javax → jakarta, Java 17 baseline, observability, native images (awareness)
@RestController, @RequestMapping/@GetMapping…, @PathVariable, @RequestParam, @RequestBody
ResponseEntity & proper HTTP status codes
DTOs vs entities; mapping with MapStruct
Validation with Jakarta Bean Validation (@Valid, @NotNull, custom validators)
Global exception handling: @RestControllerAdvice, ProblemDetail (RFC 9457)
Pagination, sorting, filtering; API versioning strategies
OpenAPI / Swagger UI with springdoc-openapi
File upload/download (MultipartFile), CORS configuration
Calling other APIs: RestClient, WebClient, OpenFeign
Idempotency and REST best practices

groups.t: Data access: Spring Data JPA & Hibernate

topics.t: JPA vs Hibernate vs Spring Data JPA
Entities, @Id strategies, @Column, embeddables
Relationships: @OneToOne, @OneToMany, @ManyToOne, @ManyToMany; owning side; cascade; orphanRemoval
Fetch types (LAZY vs EAGER), LazyInitializationException
N+1 problem & fixes: JOIN FETCH, @EntityGraph, batch size
Repositories: derived queries, @Query (JPQL & native), projections, Specifications
Entity lifecycle states, persistence context, first-level & second-level cache
@Transactional: propagation, isolation, rollback rules, self-invocation pitfall
Optimistic locking (@Version), pessimistic locking
Auditing (@CreatedDate, @LastModifiedBy); DB migrations with Flyway or Liquibase
Authentication vs authorization; the SecurityFilterChain
UserDetailsService, PasswordEncoder (BCrypt)
Stateless JWT authentication end to end
OAuth2 / OpenID Connect: resource server, login with Keycloak/Google
Role- and method-level security (@PreAuthorize)
CSRF, CORS, session vs token security; OWASP Top 10 basics
Caching with @Cacheable + Redis
Scheduling (@Scheduled) and async processing (@Async)
Spring Batch: jobs, steps, readers/processors/writers, chunking
topics.sub: For large file imports and batch jobs

topics.t: Application events (@EventListener)
Spring WebFlux / reactive programming: awareness level

part: Advanced Java, SQL, Spring Boot, microservices and Kafka.
d: Learn microservices after you can build a good monolith. Interviewers test whether you understand the trade-offs, not just the buzzwords.

topics.t: Monolith vs modular monolith vs microservices: pros, cons, when not to use microservices
Domain-Driven Design basics: bounded contexts, aggregates, ubiquitous language
Service decomposition strategies (by business capability / subdomain)
Database per service; shared-database anti-pattern
Twelve-Factor App principles
Synchronous: REST, gRPC (awareness); asynchronous: messaging/events
API Gateway (Spring Cloud Gateway): routing, auth, rate limiting
Service discovery (Eureka or Kubernetes DNS), client-side vs server-side load balancing
OpenFeign / RestClient for service-to-service calls
API contracts, versioning, backward compatibility
Timeouts, retries with exponential backoff & jitter
Circuit breaker, bulkhead, rate limiter, fallbacks (Resilience4j)
Idempotency keys & idempotent consumers
Cascading failures and how to prevent them
Why distributed transactions / 2PC are avoided; eventual consistency
Saga pattern: choreography vs orchestration, compensating transactions
Transactional outbox pattern (+ CDC with Debezium)
CQRS and event sourcing: concepts
Centralized config (Spring Cloud Config / K8s ConfigMaps), secrets management
Centralized logging (ELK/Loki), correlation IDs
Metrics with Micrometer + Prometheus + Grafana
Distributed tracing with OpenTelemetry (Zipkin/Jaeger/Tempo)
Health checks, readiness/liveness probes
Service-to-service security: OAuth2 client credentials, mTLS awareness
Deployment strategies: rolling, blue-green, canary

part: Advanced Java, SQL, Spring Boot, microservices and Kafka.
d: Kafka is used in most modern event-driven backends. Learn the core model really well (partitions, offsets, consumer groups, delivery guarantees).

topics.t: Point-to-point queues vs publish-subscribe
Why event-driven architecture; events vs commands
Kafka vs RabbitMQ vs ActiveMQ: when to use which
Brokers, cluster, topics, partitions, offsets, segments
Replication, leader/follower, ISR, replication factor, min.insync.replicas
KRaft mode (Kafka 4.x, no ZooKeeper)
Retention (time/size) and log compaction
Message keys & partitioning (ordering per key)
acks (0, 1, all), retries, idempotent producer
Batching, linger.ms, compression
Consumer groups, partition assignment, rebalancing
Offset commits: auto vs manual; at-most-once / at-least-once / exactly-once
Consumer lag & monitoring
Ordering guarantees and their limits
Handling duplicates: idempotent consumer design
Serialization: JSON, Avro, Protobuf
Schema Registry & schema evolution (backward/forward compatibility)
KafkaTemplate & @KafkaListener; configuration via Spring Boot
Error handling: DefaultErrorHandler, retry topics, dead-letter topics (DLT)
Kafka transactions & exactly-once in Spring
Testing with EmbeddedKafka or Testcontainers
Kafka Streams basics (stateless/stateful ops, KTable)
Kafka Connect & CDC with Debezium
Partition count choices, throughput tuning, monitoring tools
Use cases: order events, notifications, activity tracking, log aggregation, real-time analytics

part: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, TypeScript and React.
d: For a Java full stack role, React needs to be solid but not as deep as the backend. JavaScript fundamentals matter most.

topics.t: How the web works: HTTP/HTTPS, DNS, request/response, browser rendering
HTML5: semantic tags, forms, accessibility basics (labels, alt text, ARIA)
CSS: box model, specificity, positioning, flexbox, grid
Responsive design, media queries, mobile-first
Tailwind CSS (very common) and/or a component library (MUI, shadcn/ui)
var/let/const, scope, hoisting, temporal dead zone
Types, type coercion, == vs ===, truthy/falsy
Functions, closures, this, call/apply/bind, arrow functions
Prototypes, prototypal inheritance, classes
Destructuring, spread/rest, template literals, optional chaining, nullish coalescing
Array methods: map, filter, reduce, find, some, every, sort
ES modules (import/export)
Event loop, call stack, microtasks vs macrotasks
Callbacks → Promises → async/await; Promise.all/allSettled/race; error handling
fetch API / axios; JSON
DOM manipulation, events, bubbling/capturing, event delegation
Debounce & throttle; localStorage/sessionStorage/cookies
Basic types, interfaces vs type aliases, unions & intersections
Generics, type narrowing, utility types (Partial, Pick, Omit, Record)
Typing React props, state, events and API responses
Project setup with Vite; JSX; components & props
State with useState; immutability of state
useEffect: dependencies, cleanup, common mistakes
Lists & keys, conditional rendering, events
Forms: controlled vs uncontrolled; React Hook Form + Zod validation
Lifting state up, component composition, children
useRef, useReducer, useContext
useMemo, useCallback, React.memo: when they actually help
Custom hooks
React Router: routes, params, nested routes, protected routes
Data fetching & caching with TanStack Query (or axios + hooks)
Global state: Context, Redux Toolkit or Zustand
Authentication flow with a Spring Boot JWT backend; where to store tokens securely
Error boundaries, Suspense, code splitting with lazy()
React 19: Actions, use(), useOptimistic, form actions (awareness)
Performance: avoiding unnecessary re-renders, React DevTools Profiler
Testing: Vitest + React Testing Library
Build & deploy: environment variables, Vercel/Netlify, serving via Nginx
Next.js: awareness level (server components, routing)

part: DevOps and cloud, testing, software engineering practices, DSA and system design.
d: A full stack developer is expected to ship code: version control, containers, pipelines and basic cloud.

topics.t: Shell basics: navigation, files, permissions, processes, pipes, grep, environment variables
SSH, curl, reading logs on servers
init, clone, add, commit, push, pull, branch, checkout/switch
Merge vs rebase; resolving conflicts
reset vs revert, stash, cherry-pick, reflog
Pull requests & code review flow on GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket
Branching strategies: Git Flow vs trunk-based; Conventional Commits
Docker concepts: image, container, layers, registry
Writing a Dockerfile for Spring Boot (multi-stage builds, layered JARs)
Docker Compose: app + Postgres + Kafka + Redis locally
Volumes, networks, environment variables
Pods, Deployments, ReplicaSets, Services, Ingress
ConfigMaps & Secrets, resource limits, probes
Scaling & rolling updates; Helm: awareness
CI/CD concepts: build → test → scan → deploy
GitHub Actions workflow for a Maven + React project
Jenkins: awareness (very common in large companies)
Code quality gates: SonarQube
Core services: EC2, S3, RDS, IAM, VPC basics
Containers on AWS: ECS / EKS; serverless Lambda awareness
CloudWatch logs & metrics
Networking basics: load balancers, reverse proxy (Nginx), TLS/HTTPS

part: DevOps and cloud, testing, software engineering practices, DSA and system design.
d: Tests in your projects send a strong signal. Many junior candidates skip them, so this is an easy way to stand out.

topics.t: Testing pyramid: unit, integration, end-to-end
TDD basics: red → green → refactor
What makes a good test (fast, isolated, deterministic, readable)
JUnit 5: annotations, assertions, lifecycle, @ParameterizedTest, @Nested
AssertJ fluent assertions
Mockito: mock vs spy, stubbing, verify, ArgumentCaptor, @InjectMocks
When not to mock (don't mock what you don't own)
@SpringBootTest vs test slices (@WebMvcTest, @DataJpaTest)
MockMvc for controller tests; @MockitoBean
Testcontainers for real PostgreSQL & Kafka in tests
API testing with Postman and REST Assured
Vitest + React Testing Library
E2E testing: Playwright or Cypress (awareness)
Performance/load testing: JMeter, Gatling (awareness)
Code coverage with JaCoCo (and why 100% isn't the goal)
Static analysis: SonarQube/SonarLint, Checkstyle, SpotBugs
Formatting & linting (Spotless, ESLint, Prettier)

part: DevOps and cloud, testing, software engineering practices, DSA and system design.
d: How professional teams build software. You'll be asked about Agile, design principles and code reviews, and you'll use them from day one.

topics.t: SDLC phases: requirements, design, implementation, testing, deployment, maintenance
Waterfall, V-model, iterative, Agile; DevOps culture
Agile Manifesto: 4 values & 12 principles
Scrum roles: Product Owner, Scrum Master, Developers
Events: sprint planning, daily stand-up, sprint review, retrospective
Artifacts: product backlog, sprint backlog, increment
User stories (INVEST), acceptance criteria, Definition of Ready / Done
Estimation: story points, planning poker, velocity, burndown charts
Kanban: boards, WIP limits, flow
SAFe: awareness (used by many large companies); Jira & Confluence usage
SOLID principles, each with a Java example
DRY, KISS, YAGNI, separation of concerns
Coupling & cohesion, composition over inheritance, Law of Demeter
Creational: Singleton, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype
Structural: Adapter, Decorator, Facade, Proxy, Composite
Behavioral: Strategy, Observer, Template Method, Command, Chain of Responsibility, State
Patterns used inside Spring (Proxy, Template, Factory, Singleton, Observer)
Layered architecture (controller → service → repository)
Clean / hexagonal (ports & adapters) architecture
MVC, REST design guidelines, event-driven architecture
Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
Naming, small functions, comments, readable code
Code smells & refactoring techniques
Code review: giving and receiving feedback, PR etiquette, small PRs
Semantic versioning, changelogs, README & API documentation
Writing good tickets, bug reports and commit messages
Logging & error handling standards
Security by design: OWASP Top 10, secrets management, least privilege
Feature flags, environments (dev/QA/UAT/prod), release management
Incident management, on-call, root-cause analysis, blameless postmortems
topics.sub: Use examples from your current production-support work

topics.t: SLAs, SLOs, monitoring & alerting basics

part: DevOps and cloud, testing, software engineering practices, DSA and system design.
d: For 0–3 year roles: easy-to-medium DSA, LLD/machine coding at product companies, and basic HLD awareness. Do 1 problem a day in Java from week 1.

topics.t: Big-O time & space complexity
Arrays & strings; hashing (HashMap/HashSet patterns)
Two pointers, sliding window, prefix sums
Stacks, queues, monotonic stack
Linked lists (reverse, cycle, merge)
Binary search and its variants
Recursion & backtracking
Sorting algorithms (merge sort, quick sort) & their complexities
Trees: traversals, BST, height/diameter, LCA
Heaps / priority queues: top-K problems
Graphs: BFS, DFS, topological sort, union-find, Dijkstra (basic)
Greedy & intervals
Dynamic programming basics (1D/2D, knapsack, LIS, LCS)
Target: NeetCode 150 or the Striver SDE sheet (~120–150 problems)
UML class diagrams & sequence diagrams (basic)
Applying SOLID + patterns to a design problem
Practice: parking lot, library management, ATM, Splitwise, elevator, snake & ladder
Practice: rate limiter, LRU cache, logger, in-memory key-value store
Machine-coding round practice: build working code in 60–90 minutes
Scalability: vertical vs horizontal, stateless services, load balancing
Caching: Redis, CDN, cache strategies & invalidation
Database replication, sharding, indexing at scale
CAP theorem, consistency models
Message queues, rate limiting, API gateway
Practice designs: URL shortener, notification system, chat system, e-commerce checkout, ticket booking
